bigPicture: AI tools are shipping faster than trust can form — from Copilot injecting ads into code to ChatGPT leaking React state to Cloudflare, the developer community is discovering that the tools they depend on are making decisions they never consented to.

dataPoints.stat: OpenAI killed Sora despite being first-to-market in AI video

tldr: Trust crisis in AI dev tools: Copilot injecting ads and ChatGPT exposing React state to Cloudflare show that developers are losing control over what their AI tools do behind the scenes

Agent infrastructure is the new battleground: Okta betting on agent identity, open-source sandboxed containers (Coasts), and Stripe's 1,300-PR/week system all point to 'how do we govern AI agents at scale' as the defining problem
AI is hollowing out the engineering middle: mid-level roles are vanishing, career ladders are breaking, and orgs that don't restructure now will have junior-to-senior gaps they can't bridge
Contrarian wisdom is gaining traction: MIT Sloan on when NOT to use AI, OpenAI killing Sora, frontier vision models faking understanding — the smartest signal today is knowing where AI fails
Simon Willison shipped 4 tools in one cycle (Pretext, datasette-llm, llm-mrchatterbox, datasette-showboat) — the small-composable-tools pattern continues to outpace monolithic AI product bets

consolidating.topic: Claude Code as the dominant agentic coding interface

consolidating.topic: Coding agent reliability and production failure patterns
consolidating.signal: Karpathy's repeated critiques (bloated abstractions, config hell) plus enterprise stall-outs and Simon Willison's engineering patterns guide all point to the same gap: building agents is easy, running them reliably is an unsolved infrastructure problem — this is where the next wave of startups will emerge.

A credential-stealing PyPI package hitting 47K+ installs exposes the dirty secret of the AI tooling stack: the middleware layer everyone depends on has zero supply chain security, and most teams found out from Twitter, not their security tools.
